transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some issues at work. I'm an auditor, and... I don't know, I just keep starting follow-up items after my audits, or these mentorship events we do. I always mean to finish them right then. But... then I'll find out, you know, days later, that the final email or the review form just never actually got done. So... that's what pushed me to make the appointment.
Have you experienced this kind of difficulty finishing tasks and following through on things since you were a child or a teenager, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... I guess it's always been an issue. Since I was a kid, really. 

Even back in elementary school, my report cards usually said I was bright, but... I lost assignments a lot. Or I'd rush past small details and talk out of turn. They always noted that I needed reminders to finish my work. My mom actually still jokes about it... she says I could ace a test but completely forget the project sitting right there in my backpack. So... yeah, it's not a recent thing.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like you need to be moving, especially in situations where you're expected to sit still, such as meetings?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, in meetings, I'm usually tapping my foot under the table or clicking my pen a lot. I shift around in my chair pretty constantly. One of my colleagues actually joked that she can always hear my leg going. So... yes, I suppose I do.
Do you notice these same kinds of difficulties—losing track of tasks, restlessness—affecting other parts of your life outside of work, like at home or in personal relationships?

Um... yeah. I guess so. At home... my husband basically had to take over paying the bills. And... just other commitments I agreed to do. He... well, he can't really count on me to actually finish them reliably, so he just does it all now. 

And... I know you asked about outside of work, but... the work stuff is really getting bad. It's gotten to the point where... well, a client review was actually affected by my mistakes. All the unfinished follow-ups. I'm... I just worry people are starting to question if I can even handle this promotion I'm up for. So... yeah. It's an issue.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset inattentive symptoms plus current hyperactive/impulsive signs (fidgeting, restlessness) and impairment across both work and home settings further support a combined-presentation ADHD diagnosis, narrowing to F90.0.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports longstanding (childhood-onset) inattentive symptoms (losing track of tasks, failing to complete follow-ups, careless errors, needing reminders) combined with hyperactive-impulsive symptoms (fidgeting, restlessness, foot-tapping, pen-clicking) that persist into adulthood. Symptoms are present across multiple settings (work and home) and cause clear functional impairment (client review error, risk to promotion, spouse assuming financial responsibilities). This pattern of combined inattentive and hyperactive symptoms since childhood, with cross-situational impairment, supports a diagnosis of ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0), rather than a primarily inattentive or hyperactive-only subtype, and there is no evidence of conduct disorder or other primary mood/anxiety pathology to better explain the symptoms.
